description: Represent derived certificate expressions and local CA motifs inside an e-graph so equivalent linear combinations and repeated gadget compositions collapse to the same node. This makes R-span search reusable across many generated candidates and exposes algebraic normal forms for witness fragments.
mathematical_formalization: Terms are generated by basis atoms x e_v, edge-difference constructors, subtraction, and motif constructors. Rewrite rules encode bilinearity, support factoring, coefficient normalization, and local motif identities. An e-graph stores equivalence classes and a cost c(t)=|\mathrm{supp}(t)|+\lambda\,\#\mathrm{motifs}(t) ranks certificate derivations likely to keep r small.
analogical_connections: Certificate families as algebraic common subexpressions.
implementation_hypothesis: Saturate the algebra of local witness fragments in an e-graph, cache singleton-producing derivations, and let CA or SAT generators query the cache instead of recomputing span closure from scratch.
experiment_seed: Build the e-graph over all local motifs with n<=16, measure cache-hit rate on new generated candidates, and track whether canonicalization reduces verifier time or R size.

novelty_claim: Equality saturation becomes a linear-span compression layer specialized to arithmetic witness search rather than a general compiler backend.
differentiation: The rewrite system is tuned to singleton certificate generation and support size, not to program execution speed.
